title: BrokenSleep: Remote Power Timing Attack Exploiting Processor Idle States
problem: Modern processors support multiple C-state (idle) levels with different wake-up latencies; an attacker can remotely detect which C-state a victim processor core is in by measuring network response timing, enabling covert and side-channel communication across nodes without requiring co-location on the same machine.
motivation: Prior power-based side-channel attacks require attacker and victim to share the same physical machine, but C-state wake-up latency differences are observable through network-level timing measurements, dramatically expanding the attack surface to distributed systems.
method: BrokenSleep exploits the deterministic wake-up latency differences between processor C-states (C0 active, C1/C1E/C6 sleep) to encode information in the timing of network responses from a victim server. The attacker sends network requests and measures response latency; the victim's current C-state (determined by its workload idle pattern) is deduced from the latency profile. Both covert channel (data exfiltration across security boundaries without direct network access) and side-channel (keystroke timing inference) variants are demonstrated. The attack affects both Intel and ARM processors, exploiting standard ACPI power management without any microarchitectural vulnerability.
key_novelty: The first remote timing attack based purely on processor idle-state (C-state) wake-up latency differences, eliminating the co-location requirement of all prior power-based side-channel attacks.
contributions: BrokenSleep: first remote covert and side-channel attack exploiting CPU C-state wake-up latency differences
Demonstration of data exfiltration to remote machines without direct network access using C-state timing
Keystroke timing inference via remote C-state observation
Cross-architecture validation on both Intel and ARM processors

metrics.other: Demonstrated covert channel and keystroke timing inference over external network on Intel and ARM CPUs

baselines: prior local power side-channel attacks requiring co-location
limitations: The attack bandwidth and error rate for the covert channel are not quantified in the abstract; mitigation strategies are not discussed.
